REGCB and REECD Imple- mentation Building on earlier implementations of the WECC renewable energy models in OpenIPSL, this section incorporates the updated REGCB and REECD components introduced in the second-generation RES framework, providing improved numerical stability and more accu- rateinverterbehaviorunderweak-gridandlow-voltageconditions. TheREGCBgenerator/- converter model replaces the current-source formulation of REGC_A with a voltage-source 13 interface, addressing performance issues in low short-circuit ratio environments. As shown in Figure 2.7, injected dq-axis currents are computed from the converter’s internal voltage andimpedance,enablingmorerealisticdynamicbehaviorduringdisturbances. REGCBalso introduces enhanced current ramp-rate limits, updated prioritization between active and re- activecurrent,andalgebraiccurrent-magnitudelimitingtoimproverobustnessacrossawide rangeofoperatingconditions. The REECD electrical controller extends the earlier REEC_A/B/C models by incorporating expanded voltage-dependent limit (VDL) tables and updated current-limiting logic. Fig- ure 2.8 illustrates the Modelica implementation, where REECD processes power references and system measurements to generate active and reactive current commands. Its refined limit handling—including consistent Iqmin behavior, configurable active-power absorption through the Ke parameter, and a local current-compensation block—allows for improved representationofinverterdynamicsduringfaultsandlow-voltageevents. Together,theREGCBandREECDmodelsstrengthentheOpenIPSLrenewableenergymod- elingframeworkbyprovidinggreaterstability,enablingmorereliablesimulationandanaly- sisofinverter-basedresourcesinmodernpowersystems. TheseobservationsareconsistentwiththelinearanalysisshowninFigure2.9b,whichcom- pares the poles of the two controller configurations. The REEC_B model produces an un- stable pole pair at a higher frequency, explaining the oscillatory behavior observed in the time-domain simulation. The REECD model removes this instability and shifts the domi- nant poles to lower frequencies with positive damping, indicating slower but well-damped 15 dynamics.
